group.title: Technology basics
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A small flat computer with a screen you touch.
examples: She reads books on her {tablet}.
wrong: I keep my tablet in the fridge to eat later.

words.meaning: A mobile phone that also works like a small computer.
examples: I check my email on my {smartphone}.
wrong: My smartphone can’t make calls or open apps.

words.meaning: A phone you can carry with you anywhere.
examples: Please turn off your {cell phone} in the cinema.
wrong: My cell phone is fixed to the wall at home.

words.meaning: The sound your phone makes when someone calls you.
examples: I changed my {ringtone} to a song I like.
wrong: My ringtone is the light on the back of my phone.

words.meaning: A photo you take of yourself, usually with a phone.
examples: We took a {selfie} in front of the tower.
wrong: My friend took a selfie of me from across the street.

words.meaning: To look at many websites, one after another.
examples: I {surf the internet} for an hour every evening.
wrong: He surfed the internet with no computer or phone.

words.meaning: A small camera on a computer for video calls.
examples: Turn on your {webcam} so we can see you.
wrong: I listen to music through my webcam.

words.meaning: A thing you wear over your ears to listen to music.
examples: He listens to music with {headphones} on the train.
wrong: I wear headphones on my feet to keep them warm.

words.meaning: A piece of equipment that the sound comes out of.
examples: Turn up the {speaker} so everyone can hear.
wrong: I see pictures through the speaker.

words.meaning: A thing you speak into to make your voice louder or record it.
examples: Speak into the {microphone}, please.
wrong: I use a microphone to see in the dark.

words.meaning: The screen of a computer.
examples: My new {monitor} is very big and bright.
wrong: I type the words on my monitor with my fingers.

words.meaning: A wire that connects two machines or carries power.
examples: Plug the {cable} into the back of the TV.
wrong: I tied my hair with a computer cable.

words.meaning: A machine that copies a paper page into a computer.
examples: Put the letter in the {scanner} and press start.
wrong: I put my dinner in the scanner to cook it.

words.meaning: To copy a page or picture into a computer with a machine.
examples: Please {scan} your passport and email it to me.
wrong: I scanned the document by throwing it away.

words.meaning: The colored liquid used in pens and printers.
examples: The printer has run out of black {ink}.
wrong: I filled the car with ink at the gas station.

words.meaning: The main screen of a computer, where you see the icons.
examples: I saved the file on my {desktop}.
wrong: I put my coffee cup on my computer’s desktop screen.

words.meaning: A small picture on a screen that you click to open something.
examples: Click the {icon} to open the app.
wrong: An icon is a long sound the computer makes.

words.meaning: A document or picture kept on a computer.
examples: I sent you the {file} by email.
wrong: I opened the file and drank it.

words.meaning: The first page you see on a website.
examples: You can find our phone number on the {home page}.
wrong: The home page is the last page in a paper book.

words.meaning: One page that you can read on the internet.
examples: This {web page} has a map of the town.
wrong: I tore a web page out of my notebook.

words.meaning: The name you use to enter a website or app.
examples: Type your {username} and password.
wrong: My username is the street where I live.

words.meaning: A page with information and a photo about you on a website.
examples: I changed the photo on my {profile}.
wrong: My profile is the battery inside my phone.

words.meaning: Websites and apps where people share photos and messages.
examples: She posts pictures of her dog on {social media}.
wrong: I read social media in a paper newspaper.

words.meaning: The place where new emails arrive.
examples: I have fifty new emails in my {inbox}.
wrong: I keep my shoes in my inbox.

words.meaning: A small picture you add to a text message.
examples: She sent a smiling {emoji} to say thank you.
wrong: An emoji is a long letter written by hand.

words.meaning: A screen that you use by touching it with your finger.
examples: This laptop has a {touch screen}, so you don’t need a mouse.
wrong: A touch screen only works when nobody touches it.

words.meaning: To move your finger across a screen.
examples: {Swipe} left to see the next photo.
wrong: I swiped the screen by shouting at it.

words.meaning: To write using a keyboard.
examples: She can {type} very fast.
wrong: He typed the email using a pencil and paper.

words.meaning: To put copied words or pictures into a new place on a computer.
examples: Copy the address and {paste} it here.
wrong: I pasted the text, so it disappeared from the page.

words.meaning: To turn a computer or phone off and then on again.
examples: If the app freezes, {restart} your phone.
wrong: I restarted my laptop by closing the door.

words.meaning: To leave a website or app so others can’t use your account.
examples: Always {log out} when you use a shared computer.
wrong: I logged out so I could start reading my messages.

words.meaning: To make a machine or light start working.
examples: {Switch on} the computer and wait a minute.
wrong: I switched on the light to make the room dark.

words.meaning: To make a machine or light stop working.
examples: Please {switch off} your phone during the film.
wrong: She switched off the TV so she could watch the news.

words.meaning: To join a machine to another one or to the internet.
examples: I can’t {connect} to the Wi-Fi.
wrong: I connected the printer by keeping it far from the computer.

words.meaning: A link to the internet or between two machines.
examples: The {connection} is slow, so the video keeps stopping.
wrong: We have a good connection, so nothing will load.

words.meaning: The part inside a computer that keeps files and programs.
examples: My {hard drive} is full of photos.
wrong: I keep my lunch on my hard drive.

words.meaning: How loud a sound is.
examples: Can you turn down the {volume}? It’s too loud.
wrong: I turned up the volume to make the music quieter.

words.meaning: To turn off the sound of a phone, TV or computer.
examples: Please {mute} your microphone during the meeting.
wrong: I muted the video so I could hear it better.

words.meaning: A person who uses a computer, app or website.
examples: The app has millions of {users}.
wrong: A user is a person who never uses the app.

words.meaning: To start using the internet.
examples: I {go online} to check the weather.
wrong: I went online by turning off the internet.
